answer: A sybil-resistant economy can scale each identity's emission weight by its min-cut distance from anchor agents through non-kin attestation edges. Picture trust as a terrace system carved into onyx: a farm plants a whole grove of clones on one ledge, but edges sharing an inviter collapse in the cut, so the cluster earns one lane. Real cross-cluster edges cost graded work over epochs; splitting supply thins flow per head, and shared funding triggers joint slashing. Extra heads add social cost, not yield.
